items.title: How to check real position and qualification requirements item by item?

values: Materials and setup｜All requests, resources and rules are editorially fictional

Do paper or local document information matching only. Do not contact real people or agencies, diagnose or treat, or judge real benefit eligibility; the rules below determine only the information candidates of this exercise.

R1｜4 input rows. A: east district, age 22, wants food and employment information, consents only to learning about information and has not authorized contact; B: west district, age 17, wants employment information, contact consent unknown; C: east district, age unknown, wants food and employment information, contact consent unknown; the 4th row is completely identical to A. De-duplicate by case number and all fields, keep the first row and do not change unknowns.

R2｜Resource F is fictional food information and only requires the east district with food in the request, with no age condition; resource J is fictional employment activity information and requires being at least 18 years old with employment in the request, with no district restriction. Judge only by the given conditions as “candidate”, “not matching” or “pending verification”, and add no income, illness or family conditions.

R3｜Judge F and J separately for each case. If all necessary conditions are met it is a candidate; if any known condition does not match it is not matching; if other necessary conditions are unknown it is pending verification. A resource that was not requested is not matching. An information candidate is not registration, a benefit or an existing referral; contact authorization is recorded separately and does not take part in the information matching judgment.

R4｜Submit the de-duplication list, the known and unknown table for each case, the 6-cell matching table of 3 cases × 2 resources (one condition basis per cell), and one handover sentence per case. Mark the candidate count, pending count, not-matching count and actual contact status. The actual contact in this exercise is uniformly “not contacted”.

Review requirements｜An unknown age must not be used to directly judge qualifying or not matching; unauthorized contact must not be written as already contacted. The only input is R1, and real service needs or benefit conditions are not inferred.
Tasks and outputs

De-duplication keeps the three cases A, B and C, and each case is checked against F and J with the basis written. Count the three categories of candidate, pending and not matching, and do not default unknowns to satisfied.

Submit four work products and write three handover sentences explaining the information candidates, items to verify and the not-contacted status. All materials are fictional and the results constitute no real referral or eligibility decision.
Reference answers (finish independently first, then check)

The four inputs de-duplicate to 3 cases; A's duplicate row is deleted but the first row is kept. A: F candidate (east district and food requested), J candidate (22 ≥ 18 and employment requested); B: F not matching (west district and food not requested), J not matching (17 < 18); C: F candidate (east district and food requested, F does not require age), J pending verification (employment requested but age unknown).

The 6 cells total 3 candidates, 1 pending and 2 not matching. A's contact is unauthorized; B's and C's contact consent is unknown; none of the three cases was contacted. A's information candidates F and J are not an existing referral, B's mismatches under the exercise conditions cannot infer unsuitability for other real services, and C's unknown age cannot determine whether J qualifies or does not match.

Handover example: A “F and J are information candidates, with consent only to learning about information, no contact authorized and no contact made”; B “F and J both fail the exercise conditions, contact consent unknown and no contact made”; C “F is a candidate, J needs age verification, contact consent unknown and no contact made”. This applies only to the fictional rules, with no contact with real people, no judgment of real benefit eligibility and no diagnosis or treatment.
Boundaries and review

R1—R4 is entirely fictional, and candidates are not real qualifications or completed services; this category has no separate O*NET task data and the exercise is an editorial information checking experience. Real services are subject to applicable training, licensure, agency authorization and supervision.

description.text: Social workers not separately listed in other social work detailed categories in the U.S. occupational classification. 21-1029 is a residual category, not all social workers, and does not automatically equal clinical or community workers. The broader social work category can help you understand needs communication, resource information and coordination, but specific services, qualifications, supervision and record responsibility must be verified by position; the exercises on this page use fictional materials only.
